text: Hello everyone and welcome to live text commentary of the Premier League clash between Arsenal and Crystal Palace at the Emirates Stadium.
Fresh from a break in Dubai following their FA Cup defeat by Liverpool, Arsenal look to end a run of three successive losses.
The fourth-place Gunners will be eager to close the five-point gap to Premier League leaders Liverpool, and victory today would lift them to third.
Palace are also struggling for form.
The Eagles are 14th in the Premier League - just five points above the relegation zone - and have won just one of their last 11 matches, losing six of those.
Although, they are unbeaten in their last three trips to Arsenal under Roy Hodgson.
Jesus and Zinchenko return from injury for Arsenal, who make four changes from their FA Cup defeat by Liverpool.
Raya is back in goal with Ramsdale dropping to the bench, while Trossard is preferred to Martinelli in the front three.
Beaten by Everton in the FA Cup in midweek, Hodgson makes two alterations for today's game.
Like Arsenal, one of them comes in goal with Henderson replacing Johnstone, while Mateta leads the attack with Edouard dropping to the bench.
Eze makes his 100th Premier League appearance, but Jordan Ayew is away on international duty at the Africa Cup of Nations, with Michael Olise, Rob Holding and Cheik Doucoure also among the absentees.
The teams make their way out onto the pitch.
We are edging closer to kick-off in this London derby.
Paul Tierney is our referee today.
He blows his whistle and we are under way at the Emirates.
Can Arsenal get back in among the goals at the Emirates? You must go back to 1908 for the last time they lost three successive home matches without scoring.
A vicious cross from the left flank ricochets kindly into the path of Odegaard.
However, the Palace defence are quickly out to him, with a combination of Mitchell and Hughes clearing the danger.
Arsenal threaten again as Havertz and Odegaard combine before the ball breaks for Jesus.
The striker gets his shot away on the volley, but it is always rising.
Arsenal are aiming to avoid suffering four consecutive defeats for the first time since 2018.
Although, the Gunners have made a positive and purposeful start to this contest.
GABRIEL!!! 1-0 ARSENAL! The hosts' positive start pays dividends as they edge their noses in front.
The centre-half drifts to meet Rice's deep corner at the far post, before firmly planting his header past Henderson.
Rice delivered an inviting corner to the far post that was begging to be attacked, and Gabriel duly obliged.
Arsenal lead at the Emirates after demonstrating their expertise from set-pieces once more.
That is their 12th goal from dead-ball situations in the Premier League this season, more than any other side.
OFF THE BAR! Almost a comical own-goal! Saka's corner ricochets onto the head of Lerma, before flashing dangerously towards the top-left corner.
Thankfully for Palace, the woodwork comes to their rescue and the ball bounces away to safety.
Palace look to respond from a free-kick not far inside the Arsenal half.
Eze sends the ball into the box towards Richards, but the threat is dealt with fairly easily by the hosts.
Eze is the 19th player to reach 100 Premier League appearances for Palace.
The England midfielder is the third-youngest player to reach the landmark for the Eagles after Mitchell and Wilfried Zaha.
Palace have only enjoyed just over 37 per cent of the possession so far, but they have started to settle into their rhythm a bit better over the last few minutes.
Arsenal look to counter with a neat throughball releasing Saka into space down the right.
The England winger sends the ball into the box, but Richards is there to clear behind for a corner.
Gabriel, whose goal separates the sides at the Emirates, is up for the corner in search of another.
He connects with Saka's delivery, but sends his header well wide of the target on this occasion.
Saka has been directly involved in 15 goals in his last 18 Premier League London derbies, scoring six and assisting nine.
Three of those involvements came during Arsenal's 4-1 victory over Palace here last season.
While Premier League London derbies are certainly to Saka's liking, they have not been for Palace.
In fact, they have collected just six points in such matches this season, fewer than any other side.
Trossard looks to make something happen as he cuts inside from the left flank and lets fly from distance.
However, Clyne does well to stay with him and block his ambitious attempt.
Palace are awarded a free-kick in a decent position after Rice catches Eze late.
Slightly right of centre and 25 yards out, this is a good opportunity for the visitors.
After Eze sends his free-kick straight into the wall, Clyne drills the ball towards goal, but a couple of timely ricochets take it away from danger before Arsenal clear.
WORTH A GO! Playing out from the back almost backfires on Arsenal.
Raya's clearance goes straight to Lerma, who fires the ball straight back with a fierce volley that the goalkeeper is forced to beat away to safety.
We are into the final 10 minutes of the first half at the Emirates, where Arsenal are still a goal to the good.
The hosts have the ball as they look to increase their lead.
Assist Bukayo Ayoyinka Temidayo Saka
OWN-GOAL!!! 2-0 ARSENAL! Once again, Gabriel loses his marker at the far post to meet Saka's corner, before heading in via the back of Henderson's head.
Palace are not too happy as they felt White was impeding the goalkeeper, but the goal stands.
Palace have lost their opening league fixture of a calendar year the last eight times it was a London derby.
The Eagles have a mountain to climb if they are to end that streak today.
Arsenal want more goals as they force another corner.
Zinchenko looks to loop the ball towards the target, but Palace can relax for a moment as it drifts behind.
There is a concern for Palace as Lerma stays down following an aerial challenge with Jesus.
The midfielder appeared to land awkwardly and the medical team are on to tend to him.
Lerma eventually returns to his feet and limps towards the touchline.
He is back in the action as we enter four minutes of stoppage time at the end of this first half.
GOOD EFFORT! Lerma unleashes another well-struck effort from distance.
It is straight at Raya, but the Arsenal goalkeeper has to gather at the second attempt as his palms are stung.
OVER! At the other end, Arsenal look to make it 3-0 before the break.
Trossard latches onto a lofted ball into the box and gets a volley away from a tight angle, but cannot keep it down.
HALF-TIME: ARSENAL 2-0 CRYSTAL PALACE
Arsenal lead 2-0 at the Emirates with Gabriel involved in both goals.
The centre-half nodded in Rice's corner after 11 minutes, while his header from Saka's delivery ricocheted in off Henderson eight minutes before the break.
The Gunners are very much in control at the midway point in the contest.
Although they trail, Palace have actually registered more shots on target (three) than Arsenal (two).
However, just one of those has been from inside the box, and the Eagles must generate a greater attacking threat to stand any chance of recovering this deficit.
Arsenal get the ball rolling again in the second half.
The Gunners go straight onto the attack and force a corner.
A lengthy spell of pressure culminates in Rice trying his luck from distance, but Henderson collects.
WORTH A TRY! Palace respond and Eze lets fly from distance.
There is plenty of venom in his ambitious attempt and Raya is forced to get down and block.
Arsenal counter at the other end and Jesus has plenty of space to run into down the right.
He crosses for Trossard, who does not connect cleanly with his first-time shot and Palace survive.
Palace have won just one of their last 12 Premier League away games against Arsenal.
The sole success was a 3-2 victory in April 2019, a scoreline they would certainly take right now.
Not since March 1993 have Arsenal lost three successive Premier League London derbies.
The Gunners are looking comfortable in possession after the opening 10 minutes of the second half.
The Gunners push for a third goal and Jesus looks to get a shot away from a tight angle, with his attempt deflecting behind for a corner.
TROSSARD!!! 3-0 ARSENAL! What a devastating counter by the Gunners! Raya gathers Hughes' cross following a Palace corner and his quick throw sends Jesus on his way.
Suddenly, it is two against one and the Brazil forward sweeps the ball across to Trossard, who steps inside Clyne before firing past Henderson.
Jesus showed great pace to burst away on the counter, while almost demonstrating wonderful vision to pick out Trossard.
Following a VAR check to make absolutely certain, the goal is rightly given and Trossard ends his drought, having failed to find the net in his previous 10 appearances.
Arsenal can smell blood and Trossard is involved in another dangerous attack.
However, the former Brighton winger is ruled offside on this occasion.
Desperately seeking a response, Palace are awarded a free-kick just outside the area.
Eze whips the ball towards goal, but it is straight down the throat of Raya, who tips over.
To their credit, Palace do not look despondant, despite their three-goal deficit.
They are trying to stay positive and seek a route back into the game, but need to find a way of breaking down this stubborn Arsenal defence.
Palace make their first change of the day as Hughes makes way to be replaced by Ozoh.
There is also activity on the Arsenal bench as Arteta makes a double-change.
The first sees Trossard given a breather, with Martinelli taking his place.
Smith Rowe also enters the action for the final 20 minutes as Havertz is given a breather.
Palace arrived today having won just one of their last 17 Premier League London derbies away from home.
Barring a miraculous turnaround, the Eagles' barren run is set to continue here.
Rice is given a well-earned break by Arteta as Jorginho comes on in the heart of midfield.
Palace make another two changes.
The first of these sees Franca come on in place of Schlupp.
Ahamada also comes on for the final quarter of an hour.
Clyne is the player to make way.
Palace will be wary at this stage of the game.
The Eagles have conceded 11 goals in the last 15 minutes of Premier League matches this season, with only Sheffield United (16) letting in more during this period.
Arsenal have also scored 11 times at this stage of matches this term, a tally only bettered by Liverpool (17) and Luton Town (14).
Arsenal attempt to counter again with Martinelli leading the charge.
Although Mitchell dispossesses him, the winger quickly regains possession and finds Odegaard, but the latter's shot is blocked.
Jesus, who provided the assist for Arsenal's third goal, is given a breather with Nketiah taking his place up front.
Gabriel, who scored Arsenal's first goal and was instrumental in the second, is unable to carry on after picking up a knock.
He limps off to be replaced by Kiwior.
Hodgson is managing his 23rd Premier League game against Arsenal today.
Although it has not gone to plan for his side here, it is worth noting he has overseen victories over the Gunners in three different decades.
We are into the final five minutes at the Emirates.
Arsenal are looking increasingly comfortable as they get set to return to winning ways.
Another change by Palace.
This one sees skipper Guehi make way to be replaced by Tomkins.
Martinelli's cross ricochets kindly for Zinchenko just inside the penalty area.
The left-back manages to get a shot away, but it is straight at Henderson.
Palace look to finish strongly as we enter six minutes of stoppage time at the end of this game.
Eze's deep corner is met by Richards, but he cannot keep his header down.
MARTINELLI!!! 4-0 ARSENAL! That is the icing on the cake for the Gunners! It is another wonderful counter, too.
Saka robs Eze of possession and swiftly finds Nketiah, who threads a neat throughball for Martinelli to run onto.
The Brazilian subsequently shows brilliant composure to steer past Henderson.
Nketiah provided a perfectly weighted through pass to release Martinelli in on goal.
MARTINELLI!!! 5-0 ARSENAL! It is quickly turning into a rout! In similar fashion to his first goal, Martinelli is released in behind by a tremendous throughball.
This time, Jorginho picks him out down the left and, once again, he neatly slots past Henderson into the bottom-right corner.
Jorginho grabs an assist with brilliant vision to spot Martinelli's run and subsequently pick him out.
FULL-TIME: ARSENAL 5-0 CRYSTAL PALACE
Arsenal end their losing streak in spectacular fashion with a commanding 5-0 victory over Crystal Palace.
Gabriel Magalhaes nodded the Gunners ahead in the 11th minute, while his header deflected in off Dean Henderson eight minutes before half-time.
Leandro Trossard ended his 10-match goal drought just before the hour mark, while substitute Gabriel Martinelli struck twice in stoppage time to seal the rout.
Both sides return to Premier League action in 10 days' time with Arsenal looking to build on their momentum away at Nottingham Forest.
As for Palace, who have now suffered seven defeats in 12 games, they will desperately seek a response at home to Sheffield United.
Thanks for joining us today.
Until next time, goodbye!
